newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Queensland, NSW lead Australian economy - ABS.
newsitem.headline: Queensland, NSW lead Australian economy - ABS.

text.p: Queensland and New South Wales, the third and first most populous states, are leading the Australian economy, according to trend data issued by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Thursday.
Queensland's gross state product grew at a trend quarterly rate of 1.1 percent in constant price terms in the December quarter.
New South Wales' grew 0.9 percent in the quarter.
The national economy, measured by a different methodology, grew at a 0.4 percent or 0.6 percent trend rate in the same period, depending on the measure chosen.

The other three main states showed similar trend growth rates: 0.7 percent in Victoria and 0.6 percent in South Australia and Western Australia. heavily driven by resource developments, has vied with Queensland as the fastest-growing state.
The trend data, moving averages that iron out bumps in the highly volatile seasonally adjusted series, is subject to revision.
Further, the bureau warns that its constant-price measure is only experimental.
